from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors are directed arrows in 2D space.",
            "Vector addition uses the tip-to-tail method.",
            "Scalar multiplication scales the arrow's length."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows", lecture_lines)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        # Animation Setup
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(2, 3), color=WHITE)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=WHITE).next_to(v.get_end(), UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Showing components
        line_x = DashedLine(axes.c2p(2, 3), axes.c2p(2, 0), color=GREEN)
        line_y = DashedLine(axes.c2p(2, 3), axes.c2p(0, 3), color=GREEN)
        label_x = MathTex("x", color=GREEN).next_to(line_x.get_center(), RIGHT)
        label_y = MathTex("y", color=GREEN).next_to(line_y.get_center(), UP)
        
        self.play(Create(line_x), Create(line_y), Write(label_x), Write(label_y))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        v_scaled = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(1, 1.5), color=BLUE)
        self.play(Transform(v, v_scaled))
        self.play(FadeOut(line_x), FadeOut(line_y), FadeOut(label_x), FadeOut(label_y))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", [
            "Linear combination: scale and add vectors.",
            "Span: all points reachable by combinations.",
            "Example: robot arm's reachable 2D area."
        ])
        
        # Define vectors
        v = Vector([1, 2], color="#FF00FF")
        w = Vector([2, -1], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(w, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(Create(v), Create(w))
        a = ValueTracker(1.5)
        v_scaled = always_redraw(lambda: Vector([a.get_value() * 1, a.get_value() * 2], color="#FF00FF").move_to(self.grid['C3']))
        self.add(v_scaled)
        self.play(a.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(a.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=1)
        self.remove(v_scaled)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Parallelogram representing span
        span_area = Polygon(
            [0, 0, 0], [1, 2, 0], [3, 1, 0], [2, -1, 0],
            fill_opacity=0.3, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=0
        )
        self.place_at_grid(span_area, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(span_area))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(Flash(span_area, color=WHITE, line_length=0.2, num_lines=15))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining a Basis", [
            "Basis: vectors that are linearly independent.",
            "They span the entire space efficiently.",
            "Standard basis grid locates points precisely."
        ])

        # Objects
        # Use SVG for the grid
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        
        i_vec = Vector([1, 0], color="#FFA500")
        j_vec = Vector([0, 1], color="#FFA500")
        i_label = MathTex("\\vec{i}", color="#FFA500")
        j_label = MathTex("\\vec{j}", color="#FFA500")
        
        # Placement
        self.place_at_grid(grid_asset, "C4", scale_factor=2.0)
        # Manually adjust vector placement relative to grid origin if needed
        # The grid asset is roughly at C4.
        origin = self.grid["C4"]
        i_vec.move_to(origin + RIGHT * 0.5)
        j_vec.move_to(origin + UP * 0.5)
        i_label.next_to(i_vec, DOWN)
        j_label.next_to(j_vec, LEFT)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_asset), Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Changing color of grid asset. SVG might need VGroup decomposition if color changes fail
        self.play(grid_asset.animate.set_color("#808080"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#808080")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(i_vec), Indicate(j_vec))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Visual Connection", [
            "Span, independence, and basis are core building blocks.",
            "Losing a basis vector collapses the space.",
            "A 3D crane loses movement if vectors dependent."
        ])
        
        # Colors for highlighting
        c1, c2, c3 = "#FFD700", "#00CED1", "#FF4500"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Representing Span, Independence, Basis
        span_obj = Circle(radius=0.5, color=c1, fill_opacity=0.3)
        indep_obj = VGroup(*[Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*0.5, color=c2), Arrow(ORIGIN, RIGHT*0.5, color=c2)])
        basis_obj = VGroup(span_obj.copy().scale(0.5), indep_obj.copy().scale(0.5))
        
        self.place_at_grid(span_obj, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(indep_obj, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(basis_obj, 'B6')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(span_obj), FadeIn(indep_obj), FadeIn(basis_obj))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Collapse visualization
        plane = Square(side_length=2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'D2', 'F5')
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        
        # Shrink the plane
        self.play(plane.animate.stretch(0.1, dim=1), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(c2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Simple crane-like representation
        crane = VGroup(Line(ORIGIN, UP*1.5), Line(UP*1.5, UP*1.5+RIGHT*1)).set_color(c3)
        self.place_at_grid(crane, 'D3')
        self.play(Create(crane))
        self.play(crane.animate.rotate(PI/4, about_point=crane[0].get_start()))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(c3)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Vectors as Arrows
sections.content: Briefly define vectors as directed arrows in 2D space (R²). Visualize vector addition as the 'tip-to-tail' method and scalar multiplication as scaling the length.
sections.example: Representing a character's movement: Vector A (2 units right) + Vector B (1 unit up) = Resultant jump.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as scaling and adding vectors. Introduce 'Span' as the set of all possible points reachable by combining given vectors (a line, a plane, or the whole space).
sections.example: A robot arm with two joints: The 'Span' represents the entire reachable area (a 2D disk) the claw can touch.

sections.title: The Concept of Linear Dependence
sections.content: Explain linear dependence visually: two vectors are dependent if they lie on the same line (collinear). If a new vector adds no new 'reach' to the span, it is redundant.
sections.example: If two supply drones fly in the exact same direction, one is redundant; they don't expand the 'reach' of your delivery network.

sections.title: Defining a Basis
sections.content: Introduce Basis as the 'minimalist' set: vectors that are linearly independent (no redundancy) and span the entire space. It is the most efficient coordinate system.
sections.example: Using standard basis vectors i=(1,0) and j=(0,1) as a grid map to pinpoint the exact location of a treasure chest.

sections.title: Summary & Visual Connection
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts: Span (the reachable area), Independence (no waste), and Basis (the building blocks). Visual animation showing the collapse of a 3D space to a 2D plane if a basis vector is lost.
sections.example: A 3D crane loses a pivot; if the vectors become linearly dependent, the crane loses a dimension of movement.
